sections.title: The letter u
paragraphs: You call this letter (u) /u/. Its main sound is a vowel, heard in (uno) /ˈu.no/, which means one. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter has two sounds. It can act as a pure vowel or as a quick glide before another vowel.

sections.title: How to say u
paragraphs: Pull your tongue back and raise it high toward the roof of your mouth. Push your lips forward into a small tight circle, and keep your voice on. For the glide sound, tighten your lips very fast and move at once into the next sound. Put your hand on your throat to feel the voice buzz steadily.

sections.title: Spelling rules for u
paragraphs: This letter makes its vowel sound when it stands alone or between consonants, as in (luna) /ˈlu.na/. It becomes a glide in a diphthong before or after another vowel. A diphthong is two vowel sounds in one syllable, where the sound glides from the first to the second. You hear this quick sound in (uomo) /ˈwɔ.mo/ and in (guida) /ˈɡwi.da/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid with u
paragraphs: Do not turn this vowel into the sound heard in boot. English words often add a glide, or relax into the vowel of put. Italian keeps the sound steady and pure. Push your lips forward into a circle and do not move your tongue at all. In unstressed parts of words, never make this letter weak like the vowel in focus.
